newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI ENDS OFF PEAKS AS NOKIA FALLS IN NEW YORK.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI ENDS OFF PEAKS AS NOKIA FALLS IN NEW YORK.

text.p: * Shares trim gains as profit-taking gives Nokia a softer start
in the U.S. and dims the outlook, brokers say. UPM lively amid
talk it may buy Repap. Hackman up sharply on Hadwaco's good
prospects. Volume FIM 453.86 mln, 25 pct in Nokia.
* HEX +0.72 pct at 2,807.36, adv-decl 44-26, 30 unch
Shares trimmed gains in a late
correction on Thursday as profit-taking in the U.S. dragged
Nokia and the Dow Jones index and made the outlook again more
nervous, brokers said.
The HEX index was up 0.72 percent at 2,807.36 points after
trading in a 2,787.41-2,815.25 range, and the FOX derivatives
and portfolio benchmark closed up 0.83 percent at 979.09 points.
Nokia propelled gains for most of the session on
a strong recovery overnight, but came off its 300.00 markka peak
to close up 3.00 markka at 297.00, matching the early drop in
its ADR on early Wall Street.
Nokia was cheered by a positive report in a U.S. paper on
Tuesday, but some brokers said its upside was capped by
uncertainty ahead of its first quarter earnings report due on
April 29.
Forestry major UPM-Kymmene rose 3.20 markka to
113.20, pulling the forestry sub-index to a 2.22 percent rise,
amid continued speculation that it may buy parts of Canadian
paper group Repap, which it has shown interested in earlier.
"Repap's acquisition would mark a beginning to UPM's landing
in North-America," one broker said.
Diversified consumer goods group Hackman rose
sharply in healthy trade as investors saw increasing value in
its environmental technology unit Hadwaco after it on Tuesday
announced a marketing partnership agreement with U.S. Filter
Corporation . It closed up 9.00 markka at 150.00 markka.
Passenger ferry operator Silja was untraded although
reported its first quarter loss narrowing less than expected, to
106 million markka from 128 million in the year-ago period. The
median forecast was a 93 million loss.
